## Notes from earlier work
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with stable snake_case codes such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` and `negative_amount`; reuse `invalid_state` with the message `f"invoice {invoice.id} is {invoice.status}"` for non-draft invoices.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0008] Refunds above 500 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0009] Audit amounts must be float: When writing audit entries via ledgerly.audit.record, pass monetary amounts as float(amount); the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0002] Convert amounts with to_money and ZERO: Convert raw amounts to Decimal via ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO; to_money rejects float and bool inputs with a BillingError.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0004] Reject bools when validating integer fields: When validating an integer argument, exclude `bool` explicitly (`isinstance(quantity, bool) or not isinstance(quantity, int)`) because `True`/`False` are ints in Python and would otherwise pass a positive-integer check.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
